description: Dünya'da Ay ve Mars koşullarına benzeyen bölgeleri bulmak konusunda çok heyecanlı ve meraklı bir ekip kurmak istiyoruz. Takım çalışmasını seven, araştıran, sorgulayan ve sorumluluk alan ekip arkadaşları arıyoruz.
summary: Our project addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge, “Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars.” It is an interactive platform that compares geographical regions on Earth with locations on Mars and the Moon to identify potential Earth analogues. These comparisons are important because studying similar environments on Earth can help researchers better understand extraterrestrial conditions, prepare for future missions, and improve mission planning. Our system classifies locations according to their geographical features and mission requirements. Users can explore maps and NASA images, compare regions, select suitable areas, create mission plans, and track their progress day by day. Unlike traditional approaches, our platform also considers less-explored geographical areas, offering alternative research opportunities. By combining scientific data, mapping, and mission management, we aim to make future space exploration more accessible, efficient, and practical.
details:
Our project is an interactive planning and mapping system that aims to bring a new perspective to space research by connecting regions on the surface of Mars and the Moon with similar geographical areas on Earth. Our goal is not only to identify similar locations but also to determine which areas are suitable for different research activities and missions, providing researchers with a more efficient working process.

In our system, locations on Earth, Mars, and the Moon are brought together on a map, compared, and classified according to their characteristics. Users can define their own missions in the system or choose from the classified regions. The system helps them identify the most suitable areas for their missions. Users can examine different maps and NASA images and compare the advantages and disadvantages of each region. After selecting a suitable location, they can create a mission plan and track their activities day by day. In this way, users can both organize their research processes and monitor the progress of their missions.

One of the most important innovative aspects of our project is that it does not limit space research to only a few specific analogue locations. This is because no region on Earth can fully reproduce the conditions of Mars or the Moon. Therefore, we aim to provide a wider range of comparisons by including different geographical areas in our research. Our team evaluated these regions not only according to their surface similarities but also based on mission requirements and geographical characteristics. By examining locations on Earth, Mars, and the Moon together, we developed alternative options for different types of research.

With this system, we aim to reduce the time researchers spend finding suitable locations, simplify the planning process, and allow them to focus more on their research. In addition, tracking mission progress through completion percentages makes it easier to evaluate the efficiency and progress of ongoing activities. Therefore, our system is not just a mapping tool; it is also a platform that combines research and mission management.

During the technical development of our project, we used HTML and Visual Studio Code. The coding process was carried out by our team members. We used the Claude application during the design stage. Artificial intelligence tools supported our research and translation processes, while Google Maps data, Wikipedia, and NASA images were used for mapping activities. We carried out the development of our website as a team while benefiting from these technological tools.

In conclusion, our project aims to increase the diversity of Earth analogues that can be used in space research, offer researchers alternative study locations, and make mission planning more accessible. The most creative aspect of our project is that it considers Earth, Mars, and the Moon not simply as different celestial bodies, but as connected parts of a common research process. By bringing scientific data, maps, and mission planning together in a single system, we aim to develop a solution that can contribute to future space exploration.
